issues.body:
The entry records floor 86 for sparq-jsonld, but nothing measures the crate. `grep -c sparq-jsonld scripts/coverage.sh` returns 0: it is not in PER_COMMIT_CRATES, not in any of the three SHARD_GROUPS, and not in DEDICATED_PIPELINE_CRATES. Since the nightly/full tiers also fall back to PER_COMMIT_CRATES (selection precedence: COVERAGE_CRATES, then COVERAGE_SHARD, else PER_COMMIT_CRATES), it is measured in no tier at all.

Every gate passes while enforcing nothing, so this fails silently rather than loudly:
- `coverage.sh --check-shards` PASSES (I ran it: "3 shard(s) + 1 dedicated-pipeline crate(s) partition 35 PER_COMMIT_CRATES exactly"). It validates only the SHARD_GROUPS + DEDICATED == PER_COMMIT_CRATES partition, so a floor entry in no tier is outside its remit.
- `--check-monotonic` PASSES: check_monotonic fails only on floor_regressions or dropped_crates, never on an added crate.
- `--check` / `--check-robust` classify the crate as MISSING (in the floor, absent from the summary), fatal only under `--require-all`. No workflow passes that flag (0 hits across .github/workflows/), so the shard jobs report it missing and exit 0.

Two consequences. First, the note's claim that "CI's --check-robust is the ratchet of record" is false here: CI never produces a measurement, so no future regression can trip the gate and the robust re-measure loop cannot re-derive the number. Second, sparq-jsonld is also absent from bench/coverage-presence.json (42 crates), so it is covered by neither the percentage gate nor the presence gate. That is exactly the state the floor file's header calls impossible ("No crate is silently dropped") and the --check-shards comment calls "silently UN-GATED". Every sibling onboarded this way (sq-bif.1 fedclient/fedplan/prov, sq-bif.7 policy, sq-bif.8 algos/canon, sq-qcnn.23 reason-el/ql, sq-6vshe.4 engine-serialize/service, sq-lsp7k.1.1 forms) wired the floor entry AND tier membership together.
issues.fix_hint:
Wire the measurement half in scripts/coverage.sh, in the same commit as the floor entry:

1. Add `sparq-jsonld` to PER_COMMIT_CRATES, with a short comment in the established style noting the crate has no Cargo features, so its whole surface compiles in a default-feature build and it needs NO `case` arm in measure() (same rationale as the existing sparq-forms and sparq-algos/sparq-canon comments).
2. Add `sparq-jsonld` to exactly one SHARD_GROUPS entry. This is mandatory, not optional: in PER_COMMIT_CRATES with no shard, `coverage.sh --check-shards` fails loudly with "PER_COMMIT_CRATES crate(s) missing from every shard AND the dedicated pipeline (would be silently UN-GATED)" -- the guard working as designed. Prefer the cheapest of the three shards and keep per-shard wall-clock balanced (LPT-packed at ~336s each; the slowest sets the floor).
3. Re-run `bash scripts/coverage.sh --check-shards` to confirm the invariant reports OK with 36 PER_COMMIT_CRATES.
4. Confirm the seed from the wired path, e.g. `COVERAGE_CRATES=sparq-jsonld scripts/coverage.sh && python3 scripts/coverage-gate.py --check target/coverage/coverage-summary.json`, so the recorded 88.73 / floor 86 is reproducible by the lane that will enforce it.

If leaving the crate unmeasured is deliberate for this bead (e.g. deferred on wall-clock grounds), the entry must not claim "CI's --check-robust is the ratchet of record". Either mirror the documented artifact convention (floor 0 + a note explaining why the number is not gated + a bench/coverage-presence.json entry so it is presence-gated), or add the floor entry only once the tier wiring lands, filing a bead for the follow-up so the crate is not left outside both gates.
issues.title: Floor seeded for sparq-jsonld but the crate is measured by no CI lane, so the ratchet is never enforced (silently un-gated)

verdict.summary:
The diff adds one bench/coverage-floor.json entry seeding a line-coverage floor of 86 for sparq-jsonld. Both verifiable claims in the note hold: the arithmetic is internally consistent (5646/6363 = 88.7317%, floor(88.73) - 2 = 86, matching the documented formula with margin_points = 2), and "the crate defines no Cargo features" is accurate today (crates/sparq-jsonld/Cargo.toml has no [features] table, so no measure() case arm is needed). The claimed 88.73% is plausible for the crate's size (~14.9k src LOC, 303 #[test] fns, a tests/ dir, plus a test=true example); I did not re-run coverage.sh to reproduce it. The file stays valid JSON and the entry is correctly alphabetised between sparq-introspect and sparq-mpc.

The change is nonetheless INCOMPLETE, silently rather than loudly. sparq-jsonld is measured by no lane: grep -c sparq-jsonld scripts/coverage.sh returns 0, so it is absent from PER_COMMIT_CRATES, from all three SHARD_GROUPS, and from DEDICATED_PIPELINE_CRATES. The nightly/full tiers also fall back to PER_COMMIT_CRATES, so it is measured nowhere. Every gate then passes while enforcing nothing: --check-shards passes (verified by running it; it validates only the PER_COMMIT_CRATES partition, untouched here), --check-monotonic passes (it fails only on lowered/dropped floors, not additions), and --check/--check-robust classify the crate as MISSING, fatal only under --require-all, which no workflow passes (0 hits in .github/workflows/). The floor is therefore decorative, making the note's own assertion that "CI's --check-robust is the ratchet of record" false for this crate. sparq-jsonld is also absent from bench/coverage-presence.json (42 crates), so it sits under neither the percentage gate nor the presence gate -- the condition the floor file's header asserts cannot happen ("No crate is silently dropped"). Every sibling precedent cited in coverage.sh (sq-bif.1, sq-bif.7, sq-bif.8, sq-qcnn.23, sq-6vshe.4, sq-lsp7k.1.1) wired both halves in one change.
